temporal_path_closure_audit.method: For each cutoff, LEFT JOIN every child *_as_of view to its corresponding parent *_as_of view and count non-null child keys with no visible parent.
temporal_path_closure_audit.cause: Per-table masks combine different availability and validity clocks; old sessions can expire while immutable historical rolls remain visible, and parents may be observed after children whose availability was backfilled to event dates.
temporal_path_closure_audit.assessment: The row predicates behave mechanically but cannot serve as a point-in-time graph/path oracle until a referential-closure policy is defined and tested.

hard_kill_criteria: Kill a transition family unless the same durable ID has retained official before state, an official event or update specification, and retained official after state.
Kill an independent-witness claim when both representations are emitted by the same build, share the same artifact lineage, or are serializations of one fetch.
Count copying, renaming, masking, exact joins, SQL group-bys, regex/template classification, sorting, set difference, and hashing as at most one procedure each, regardless of row count.
Kill a repair family unless an independent authoritative source determines the winner; unresolved conflict detection is not repair.
If the later snapshot is supplied, call the task CDC; if it is withheld and the change is a human event, call the target unknowable rather than replayable.
Kill temporal-maintenance claims based on one retrospective observation with event dates backfilled as availability.
Kill point-in-time graph/path tasks until the cutoff contract defines and enforces referential closure across parent and child relations.
Kill schema-migration claims based only on optional columns across unrelated sessions without a witnessed schema-version event.
Kill task-family scale claims unless held-out splits vary the required procedure or source schema, not merely jurisdiction, row, ID, cutoff, or mask.
Kill the compiler thesis for legal-agent RL unless at least three non-isomorphic families survive these tests with procedure-level held-out splits. Current count is zero.
